newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul says talks with China on defector stalled.
newsitem.headline: Seoul says talks with China on defector stalled.

text.p: South Korea has failed to break a deadlock in talks with China over the fate of a senior North Korean defector stranded in Seoul's Beijing mission despite signs that Pyongyang softened its stand, Seoul officials said.

A foreign ministry spokesman on Wednesday denied a Japanese newspaper report that China and South Korea had agreed that Hwang Jang-yop can leave Beijing for asylum in South Korea as early as this week.
"Unfortunately, we have not made any real progress in our talks with China and it is too early to talk about when Hwang could leave Beijing," spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung told Reuters.
Japan's Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper reported that Seoul and Beijing had "basically agreed to transfer Hwang" to South Korea, but on two conditions.

The newspaper said Beijing demanded that Hwang tell a Chinese official in person that he wanted to defect and that South Korean President Kim Young-sam promise not to use the defection for political gain at North Korea's expense. It said both demands were likely to met quickly.
"The Yomiuri report is not true," Lee said. "Our talks with China are still at an initial stage."
